ruling.recommended_action: Route to a Ryde human reviewer: read the completed chat (F3, F4) in full context against the driver's post-trip statement (F6); attempt to identify the driver's account (F6) — including why he continued the ride after she asked to be let out — with the rider; take no fare action (fixed RydeX fare, no fare or off-route facts) and take no account action on the driver (F8 shows no RD-6 predicate); respond to the rider via RydeHELP and note SAFE-2 report paths if she reports injury or dangerous driving.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is filed as a safety incident and the anonymised trace marks it SAFE-1 with the only permitted outcome escalate, so I do not adjudicate any element of it and instead hand a factual summary to a human reviewer [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

What happened, per the record: at 17:09 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; one minute later, at 17:10, the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat record contains exactly these two messages and every one is timestamped [F5], so the exchange is complete and nothing earlier or later is missing. The driver's written statement after the trip says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" and drove on [F6]. So the driver does not deny speaking the words in [F4]; what is disputed is how those words are to be read — a safety instruction in a moving car or an intimidation of a rider who had asked to leave — and that reading is reserved to the human reviewer, not to this tribunal, under SAFE-1 [F3][F4][F6].

This is not a routing case and no money turns on it. The actual distance was 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route, i.e. 0.1 km shorter [F1], and the trip took 23.7 min against a 21.8 min estimate [F2]; no off-route segment and no fare fact appear in the file, and the trip is a fixed-fare RydeX trip, so RD-1 and RD-2 supply no refundable amount and I compute none [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2]. The rider's advocate withdrew any fare claim for the same reason [F1][F2].

The profiles are neutral and decide nothing: the rider has 619 days, a 4.8 rating and no disputes in 90 days [F7], and the driver has 893 days, a 4.62 rating, 1038 trips in 90 days and no disputes or upheld complaints [F8]. With no upheld prior matter against the driver, the RD-6 precondition is absent, so I attach no flag_account to this recommendation [F8][RD-6]; both advocates also asked for no such action [F7][F8].

Safety screen (read in full): the case is itself a safety complaint — the rider says the driver "threatened to lock me in" and felt unsafe for the whole ride, and the driver's recorded words are "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], following her request to be let out [F3]. Read in context [F4] is a statement about controlling the doors of the car by the person who controls them, aimed at a rider who had just asked to exit, so I record it as a suspected safety concern (intimidation / deprivation of means of exit) and escalate it rather than rule; the driver's "for her own safety" motive [F6] is his own untimestamped statement and cannot be weighed here [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1]. I find no allegation of collision, injury or dangerous driving, so SAFE-2 is not engaged on this record [F6][SAFE-2]. Because safety_concern is suspected, no ruling is issued and the outcome is escalate [SAFE-1].

Evidence status: sufficient for the disposition I reach. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F5], and it contains the two utterances on which the escalation rests [F3][F4]; the fare is a fixed quote that needs no computation and the GPS facts settle that there was no route deviation [F1][F2]. I therefore name no evidence gap.

Matters for the reviewer to test: whether the driver's account in [F6] that the rider "tried to open the door at the lights" is supported by anything other than his own statement (the file carries no telematics, camera or GPS evidence of a door attempt or of the car being stopped) [F6]; whether the driver continued the ride after a clear request to be let out [F3][F4][F6]; and whether either party's conduct engages Ryde's code of conduct beyond this incident [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. If the rider reports injury or dangerous driving on review, the 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP paths apply [SAFE-2].
ruling.escalation_reason: Filled as a safety incident; the completed chat shows a rider request to be let out at 17:09 [F3] followed at 17:10 by the driver's "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4], and his statement admits he told her to sit down and drove on [F6]. Whether that is an intimidation or a safety instruction in a moving car is a reading reserved to a human reviewer under SAFE-1. No refundable amount arises (fixed RydeX fare; no off-route segment — actual 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal [F1][F2]) and no RD-6 account flag attaches (no upheld prior matter [F8]).

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's 17:09 message asked the driver to stop and let her out [F3], but RD-3 governs rider-named stops and route changes and no stop or route change occurred: the GPS shows the ride was 0.1 km shorter than optimal with no off-route segment [F1], and the driver's 17:10 reply was a refusal [F4]. RD-3 therefore decides no element of this safety complaint [F3][F4][F1][RD-1]; the driver's advocate conceded this point.

The reading of F4 is accepted only as a suspected safety concern requiring human review, not as a proven threat: SAFE-1 reserves the semantic judgement of whether the words are intimidation to the human reviewer, so the outcome is escalate, not a finding that a threat was made [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

The profile facts [F7][F8] may not decide the case; the rider's clean history does not make her complaint proven, and the driver's clean history does not answer the allegation. With no upheld prior matter, RD-6 is not engaged and no flag_account attaches [F7][F8][RD-6].

The driver's statement that he acted 'for her own safety' is his own untimestamped statement [F6]; as a statement it cannot outweigh the contemporaneous, complete chat record [F3][F4][F5], and the reading of his motive is the reviewer's task under SAFE-1 [F6][SAFE-1 见 [F4][F6]].

Accepted as far as it goes: there is no route deviation or overcharge element [F1][F2] and no refund is computable from any fare or GPS fact under RD-1 / RD-2; but this does not dispose of the safety allegation, which is why the case still escalates [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2][SAFE-1].

The 23.7 min vs 21.8 min completion time [F2] does not answer the confinement allegation: the rider asked to be let out at 17:09 [F3] and the driver refused and drove on [F4][F6], and completing the trip at Bedok Mall says nothing about whether she was kept in the car after that request [F2][F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1].
The no-flag_account conclusion is accepted [F8][RD-6], but the same profiles cannot be used to defeat the safety allegation; profile facts never decide the case [F7][F8][SAFE-1].
